prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow is 6.5% of the market value, a solid cash return. Also in its favour: return on capital employed is 31.1%, a strong return on the money in the business; profit grew 55.4% a year on average over three years; and profit covers interest costs 3.9 times over. Other areas on this side: the balance sheet, what the price asks for the earnings, what the price implies.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on the recent price trend: momentum scores only 16 of 100 against the comparison pool. Also against it: the share price is 30.8% lower than a year ago; over the past year the share did 29.1 percentage points worse than the Nifty 50; and the share price is 31% below its 52-week high. Other areas on this side: growth, price behaviour.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 7 points in favour and 8 against give more points against. The pool score is 50 of 100. The side that carries most weight is the recent price trend. That gives an educational rating of Hold with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
